direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is cute and feel-good as it helps capture the loneliness in a foreign country; the direction on a microscale is pretty good and does a good job invoking emotions out of you as you empathize with the characters, which is all you can ask for in a feel-good movie; the storytelling is pretty basic as it uses your emotional investment in the characters to keep you drawn in; they use your emotional attachment to the characters and story to build tension

performance.comments: Plays this lovable character that really suits his real world persona as you just want to give him a hug and show him he is not alone; has good chemistry with the cast
Plays his role well and has good chemistry with the cast
Really enjoyed her performance as her dynamic with Fraser was really entertaining and show a lot for both of their characters
Very cute and feels like the emotional compass for the movie; has a good dynamic with Fraser

cast.comments: The movie does a pretty good job at having Fraser be a heliocentric character that everyone else orbits around as they all play off his energy to help bring out the emotions in the story

story.comments: The concept is pretty interesting as it uses this concept of renting actors to be real people to explore people's lives, their insecurities, and their loneliness; the plot structure has these different sub-plots that converge every now and then with Fraser, but it felt like this mad the movie drag a bit as you could have easily shortened some of the weaker plot lines to shave 20 minutes; character writing is a strong point for this movie as the movie explores Fraser's loneliness in a foreign city he is trying to acclimate himself into, and how he makes these connections with people by being artificially placed into their lives

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty heartwarming; the symbolism is pretty good as it touches on topics like loneliness in a way I find films rarely do; the foreshadowing is pretty formulaic and predictable

cinematography.comments: Does a good job contrasting the protagonist in such a big and busy city like Tokyo; does show some of the beauty of the country

production_design.comments: Shows the beauty and serenity of Japan, acting as a character that the protagonist has to assimilate into

review.pacing: Pacing is fine for the first half, but really drags in the second half (they could have cut 20 minutes by shortening some of the unnecessary storylines)
review.climax: Climax is pretty emotionally satisfying as you feel like the protagonist has finally found a sense of closure and community
review.tone: Tone is very feel-good and heartwarming
review.overall: Overall, 'Rental Family' is a feel-good movie that uses Brendan Fraser as a heliocentric character for other characters to revolve around as he uses these artificial relationships he creates to explore his own character's loneliness in an accurate way I rarely see in films; while the movie does drag in the second half due to some unnecessary storylines, the relatable character writing and heartwarming tone make this movie an entertaining watch with the family
